fixes.explanation: Yep, baker. The psalmist says, "Your statutes are songs to me in the house of my pilgrimage." He says God's statutes are songs to him, right there in the house of his pilgrimage. I hum while I stamp, and my mustache sways along.

Not half, baker. The psalm says he has sought God's face with his whole heart, nothing held back. Right after that he asks God to be gracious to him according to His promise. So the verse leaves no room for a half-hearted seeker.
Right, that one's false. He tells God he has sought His face with all his heart, no half measures. Then he asks for grace according to God's promise. That's a man who gave it his all, baker.
Right, baker, it's false. The psalmist says, "I hurried without hesitating to keep Your commandments." He hurried, and the verse adds that he didn't hesitate. Taking his time is not what he says.
